cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine close October's books for HANGS Construction.
First it reads the trial balance: a list of every account's balance at month-end.
Then the recurring entries, the close checklist and the close procedures.
Next it spreads prepaid costs, like insurance and rent, over the months they cover.
About $3,200 of insurance was taken twice.
Then it recomputes depreciation, spreading each asset's cost over its useful life.
An excavator worth $68,500 is in the ledger but missing from the asset register.
Now accruals: October costs that are paid later, like wages for the last week of the month.
An October bill of about $12,500 arrived in November, so it's accrued.
Every entry balances to the cent.
It writes the workpapers and an unsigned memo, with about $18,000 of adjusting entries proposed.
All done. Eight entries proposed, four exceptions for a person, and two checklist items still open. Nothing was posted; the controller reviews and approves each entry.
Jumping to the results. A person still reviews every item before anything is posted, paid or sent.
